Fix #81681

@Jozkee thanks for the review and suggestions. I've pushed a new commit that implements them. The only thing I held off was the still unresolved comment around always setting `wShowWindow` and the `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` flag if `ProcessWindowStyle.Normal` was used. While I don't think it would break anything I'm not confident enough to say it won't and so just preserved the existing behaviour today. I can definitely change it to always set the flag if that's truly what is desired, on the plus side it will align with the `ShellExecute` behaviour so that could be a positive.
Thanks @Jozkee for your help in fixing this.

issue_context.title: Support WindowStyle without UseShellExecute in ProcessStartInfo and Process implementation on Windows
issue_context.body:
In PowerShell repository we have to use pinvoke to support WindowStyle without UseShellExecute.

Today .Net supports WindowStyle only if UseShellExecute is true
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/58719ec90b3bbae527dd81685bf8670b993fe8f9/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/src/System/Diagnostics/Process.Win32.cs#L23-L30

Current request is to add support for WindowStyle (on Windows) if UseShellExecute is false
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/58719ec90b3bbae527dd81685bf8670b993fe8f9/src/libraries/System.Diagnostics.Process/src/System/Diagnostics/Process.Windows.cs#L427

It looks like a very simple implementation.
We would like confirmation soon from the .Net team that this can be implemented in .Net 8 so that we can avoid unnecessary work in the PowerShell repository.

Sounds like this is just setting wShowWindow on the [STARTUPINFO](https://learn.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/processthreadsapi/ns-processthreadsapi-startupinfoa) structure we pass to CreateProcess, applying the same mapping we do on StartWithShellExecuteEx. If so, a PR would be very welcome.

Should it be invalid to allow ProcessStartInfo.WindowStyle with ProcessStartInfo.CreateNoWindow?

> Should it be invalid to allow ProcessStartInfo.WindowStyle with ProcessStartInfo.CreateNoWindow?

PowerShell throws in the case.
@iSazonov are you interested in working on this?
Maybe @jborean93 grab this. If no I will look a few weeks later.
I can certainly try if I have time.

I've opened a draft PR https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/82662. I need to figure out how to build and run the tests so I can add some tests for this new addition. I'm unsure where the docs for https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.diagnostics.processstartinfo.createnowindow?view=net-7.0#system-diagnostics-processstartinfo-createnowindow live to add an entry stating `CreateNoWindow` cannot be true if the `WindowStyle` is not `Normal`.

> I need to figure out how to build and run the tests s

```cmd
# to build the whole repo
.\build.cmd -rc Release -subset clr+libs+libs.tests
# to rebuild the library
.\dotnet.cmd build .\src\libraries\System.Diagnostics.Process\System.Diagnostics.Process.sln
# to run the tests
.\dotnet.cmd build .\src\libraries\System.Diagnostics.Process\tests\System.Diagnostics.Process.Tests.csproj /t:Test
```

Thanks for the guides, was able to add some tests. It seems like CI is failing with some problems with the `Http.Functional.Tests` which seem unrelated (it's also failing on the Linux side).

> 2023-03-02T05:18:29.5576910Z D:\a\_work\1\s\.packages\microsoft.dotnet.helix.sdk\8.0.0-beta.23123.2\tools\Microsoft.DotNet.Helix.Sdk.MultiQueue.targets(90,5): error : Work item System.Net.Http.Functional.Tests in job bba582ab-b7c6-4367-ab20-af65211d971e has failed. [D:\a\_work\1\s\src\libraries\sendtohelixhelp.proj]

As for the behaviour of `CreateNoWindow` with `WindowStyle` being set I've had to remove the exception as there was code internally that was setting both and it would break anybody else that might be accidentally setting both currently. So for now the `WindowStyle` will set the entry in the STARTUPINFO structure at the same time as `CreateNoWindow`.

review_comments:
@iSazonov was suggesting that this combined with a WindowStyle != Normal should throw. But that would be a breaking change.

I lean more towards letting the OS decide whether is an error or not. i.e: to do nothing. I just wanted to point out that this is a deliberate decision.
I just saw your comment https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/81681#issuecomment-1451353923 talking about this.
Is this meant to avoid a breaking change in the default path? Maybe it is a breaking change worth taking.
Actually, the current behavior looks just like as if we were using ProcessWindowStyle.Normal. So, we can safely map ProcessWindowStyle.Normal => SW_SHOWNORMAL.

So specifically this is done to preserve the existing behaviour where `ProcessWindowStyle.Normal` then no `wShowWindow` value is set alongside the `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` flag that tells Windows to use the value for `wShowWindow`. I'm not confident that explicitly setting the normal window style is the same as not setting it at all which is what `Normal` currently means so I kept it out. I can change the code so it always just sets this value alongside `STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW` if that's your wish but I was aiming for behaviour that was as close to what it was today.

> this is done to preserve the existing behaviour where ProcessWindowStyle.Normal then no wShowWindow value is set alongside the STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW flag.

@iSazonov would your scenario still be covered?

PowerShell [always sets the window](https://github.com/PowerShell/PowerShell/blob/66a89826bbaa7bb35c2938c3afc7785c469dbaba/src/Microsoft.PowerShell.Commands.Management/commands/management/Process.cs#L2407-L2430) so it would technically be a behaviour change on their end. It really depends on whether dotnet wants to be the one to change the behaviour or let PowerShell do it.

It would make sense for dotnet to align to the same behaviour as `UseShellExecute = true` but I'm just not confident enough to say whether this really matters or not.
Let's keep it this way to avoid the breaking change. We can change it later based on user feedback ie: if someone needs this flag to be set for a specific use case.
